arxiv-2109-03680.title: ON SOME GENERALIZATIONS TO FLOOR FUNCTION IDENTITIES OF RAMANUJAN
arxiv-2109-03680.creator: Andrzej Kukla, Sai Teja Somu
arxiv-2109-03680.description: Abstract We give some generalizations to three identities of Srinivasa Ramanujan involving greatest integer function. 1 Introduction Let \lfloor x\rfloor denote greatest integer less than or equal to x , Ramanujan proposed three interesting identities involving greatest integer function as a problem to the Journal of the Indian Mathematical Society .

arxiv-2302-04697.title: Feb 2023 Schur-like index of the Klebanov-Witten theory via the AdS/CFT correspondence
arxiv-2302-04697.creator: Shota Fujiwara
arxiv-2302-04697.description: Abstract We calculate an unrefined limit of the superconformal index (the Schur-like index) of the Klebanov-Witten theory from the dual AdS side by using the recently developed giant graviton expansion method. Our formula includes multiple sums of the contribution of the D3-branes wrapped on three-cycles in the internal space.

arxiv-2303-15405.title: Gillespie algorithm for quantum jump trajectories
arxiv-2303-15405.creator: Marco Radaelli, Gabriel T. Landi, Felix C. Binder
arxiv-2303-15405.description: Abstract The jump unravelling of a quantum master equation decomposes the dynamics of an open quantum system into abrupt jumps, interspersed by periods of coherent dynamics when no jumps occur. Such open quantum systems are ubiquitous in quantum optics and mesoscopic physics, hence the need for efficient techniques for their stochastic simulation. Numerical simulation techniques fall into two main categories.

arxiv-2407-11778.title: Local Feature Selection without Label or Feature Leakage for Interpretable Machine Learning Predictions
arxiv-2407-11778.creator: Harrie Oosterhuis, Lijun Lyu, Avishek Anand
arxiv-2407-11778.description: Abstract Local feature selection in machine learning provides instance-specific explanations by focusing on the most relevant features for each prediction, enhancing the interpretability of complex models. However, such methods tend to produce misleading explanations by encoding additional information in their selections. In this work, we attribute the problem of misleading selections by formalizing the concepts of label and feature leakage.

arxiv-2410-01050.title: Steering Elongate Multi-legged Robots By Modulating Body Undulation Waves Thanks: B. Chong and D. I. Goldman are with the School of Physics, Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, 30332 USA. Email: bchong9@gatech.edu , daniel.goldman@physics.gatech.edu Thanks: Corresponding author: Daniel I.
arxiv-2410-01050.creator: Esteban Flores, Baxi Chong, Daniel Soto, Daniel I. Goldman
arxiv-2410-01050.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Esteban Flores, Baxi Chong, Daniel Soto, Daniel I. Goldman. Centipedes exhibit great maneuverability in diverse environments due to their many legs and body-driven control. By leveraging similar morphologies and control strategies, their robotic counterparts also demonstrate effective terrestrial locomotion. However, the success of these multi-legged robots is largely limited to forward locomotion; steering is substantially less studied, in part because of the difficulty in coordinating a high degree-of-freedom robot to follow predictable, planar trajectories.

arxiv-2411-17809.title: Transdimensional Defects
arxiv-2411-17809.creator: Elia de Sabbata, a , c {\!}{}^{a,c} Nadav Drukker, c {\!}{}^{c} Andreas Stergiou c eliadesabbata@gmail.com nadav.drukker@gmail.com andreas.stergiou@kcl.ac.uk
arxiv-2411-17809.description: Abstract This note introduces a novel paradigm for conformal defects with continuously adjustable dimensions. Just as the standard ε \varepsilon expansion interpolates between integer spacetime dimensions, a new parameter, δ \delta , is used to interpolate between different integer-dimensional defects.

arxiv-2506-05609.title: Luciano Ribeiro Galvão
arxiv-2506-05609.description: Abstract Non-Heuristic Selection via Hybrid Regularized and Machine Learning Models for Insurance Abstract In this study, machine learning models were tested to predict whether or not a customer of an insurance company would purchase a travel insurance product. For this purpose, secondary data provided by an open-source website that compiles databases from statistical modeling competitions were used.

arxiv-2512-01848.title: Beyond SFT: Reinforcement Learning for Safer Large Reasoning Models with Better Reasoning Ability
arxiv-2512-01848.creator: Jinghan Jia Nathalie Baracaldo Sijia Liu
arxiv-2512-01848.description: Abstract Large reasoning models (LRMs) extend large language models by generating explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, significantly improving mathematical and logical problem solving. However, this explicit reasoning process also introduces new safety risks, as unsafe behaviors often emerge within intermediate reasoning trajectories, even when final answers appear harmless.

arxiv-2602-03235.title: Search for the production of dark Higgs in the framework of Mono-Z ′ portal at the FCC-ee simulated electron-positron collisions at s = 240 \sqrt{s}=240 GeV arXiv: arXiv:7228004 [hep-ph]
arxiv-2602-03235.creator: S. Elgammal, N. De Filippis
arxiv-2602-03235.description: Abstract In the present work, we study the possible production of the dark Higgs boson ( h D h_{D} ) candidates, which originated from a simplified-model scenario based on the Mono-Z ′ model, in association with a neutral gauge boson (Z ′ ).

pmc-10594148.title: Corticotropin Stimulation in Adrenal Venous Sampling for Patients With Primary Aldosteronism
pmc-10594148.creator: Shumin Yang, Zhipeng Du, Xizi Zhang, Qianna Zhen, Xiaoyu Shu, Jun Yang, Ying Song, Yi Yang, Qifu Li, Jinbo Hu
pmc-10594148.description: This randomized clinical trial evaluates whether treatment decisions based on adrenal venous sampling conducted with vs without corticotropin (ACTH) stimulation lead to different clinical outcomes among patients with primary aldosteronism. Introduction Primary aldosteronism (PA) is a common form of secondary hypertension.

pmc-10654435.title: Recurrence prediction of lung adenocarcinoma using an immune gene expression and clinical data trained and validated support vector machine classifier
pmc-10654435.creator: Yingran Shen, Chandra Goparaju, Yang Yang, Benson A Babu, Weiming Gai, Harvey Pass, Gening Jiang
pmc-10654435.description: BackgroundImmune microenvironment plays a critical role in cancer from onset to relapse. Machine learning (ML) algorithm can facilitate the analysis of lab and clinical data to predict lung cancer recurrence. Prompt detection and intervention are crucial for long-term survival in lung cancer relapse.

pmc-11630731.title: In reply: espying sarcopenia in gastric cancer: squaring the circle
pmc-11630731.creator: Wing-Lok Chan
pmc-11630731.description: This letter to the editor continues the discussion on sarcopenia in gastric cancer. Thank you for your insightful feedback1 on our recent publication examining the association between sarcopenia, measured by skeletal muscle index (SMI) on computed tomography (CT), and clinical outcomes in patients with advanced gastric cancer.

pmc-11674704.title: RETRACTED: Pneumonia in Patients with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treated with Venetoclax-Based Regimens: A Real-World Analysis of the Polish Adult Leukemia Group (PALG)
pmc-11674704.creator: Elżbieta Kalicińska, Paula Jabłonowska-Babij, Marta Morawska, Elżbieta Iskierka-Jażdżewska, Joanna Drozd-Sokołowska, Ewa Paszkiewicz-Kozik, Łukasz Szukalski, Judyta Strzała, Urszula Gosik, Jakub Dębski, Iga Andrasiak, Anna Skotny, Krzysztof Jamroziak, Tomasz Wróbel, Spencer Bruce B Gibson
pmc-11674704.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryThis multicenter study assessed the incidence of pneumonia and its impact on survival in 322 patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) who were treated with venetoclax-based regimens. In real-world settings, patients with CLL who are treated with venetoclax-based regimens are at a higher risk of pneumonia, especially patients with R/R CLL who are treated with venetoclax in combination with rituximab compared to registration trials.

pmc-12468537.title: Proteomic Identification of IL4I1 as a Therapeutic Target in P53-Mutant Endometrial Cancer
pmc-12468537.creator: Hu Li, Ruonan Zhang, Tiantian Sui, Kai Wang, Yiran Li, Xuezhen Luo, Qizhi He, David Mutch
pmc-12468537.description: Simple SummaryEndometrial cancer is one of the most common cancers affecting women. Among its types, those with changes in a gene called P53 tend to be more aggressive and harder to treat. Current treatment options are often not effective for these patients, and new strategies are urgently needed.

pmc-12521793.title: D1 Receptor Agonist Ameliorates Synaptic and Behavioral Deficits in a Shank3‐Deficient Mouse Model of Autism
pmc-12521793.creator: Jun‐Sik Kim, Sukmin Han, Mihyeon An, Jinsu Park, Yeongyeong Lee, Jeein Lim, Sung Hyun Kim, Dong‐Gyu Jo
pmc-12521793.description: al signaling remain poorly understood. In this study, we revealed that loss of Shank3 impairs D1 receptor–mediated cortico‐striatal projections, giving rise to ASD‐like behavioral phenotypes. Notably, pharmacological activation of the D1 receptor with SKF‐82958 restored synaptic function and ameliorated repetitive and social behavioral deficits in Shank3‐deficient mice.

pmc-12532414.title: Integrative research and innovation strategy for rare diseases. Insights from the 5-year European joint programme on rare diseases, including analysis to inform recommendations for future actions
pmc-12532414.creator: María del Carmen Sánchez-González, Rodrigo Sarmiento-Suárez, Laura Lee Cellai, Clément Moreau, Marcin Bartoszewicz, Piotr Fiedor, Domenica Taruscio, Marta de Santis, Manuel Posada de la Paz, Daria Julkowska, Claudio Carta, Eva Bermejo-Sánchez
pmc-12532414.description: BackgroundThe European Joint Programme on Rare Diseases (EJP RD) was an initiative that sought to integrate different rare disease strategies into a research ecosystem. This paper summarizes the work of the dedicated work package on Integrative Research and Innovation Strategy and outlines recommendations to facilitate alignment with National Plans and Strategies for Rare Diseases.

pmc-12650666.title: Molecular Mechanisms of the Ubiquitin-Specific Proteases (USPs) Family in Biliary Tract Cancer and Targeted Intervention Strategies
pmc-12650666.creator: Qian Cheng, Delin Ma, Shengmin Zheng, Jialing Hao, Gang Wang, Yanbin Ni, Jiye Zhu
pmc-12650666.description: Biliary tract carcinoma (BTC) is a group of highly heterogeneous malignancies arising from the biliary epithelium. Anatomically, BTC is categorized into gallbladder cancer (GBC) and cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), with the latter further subdivided into intrahepatic (iCCA), perihilar (pCCA), and distal cholangiocarcinoma (dCCA).

pmc-12651438.title: T Cell Exhaustion in the Cervical Cancer Tumor Microenvironment: PD-1 Overexpression and Co-Expression with TIGIT, Tim-3, LAG-3, and NKG2A
pmc-12651438.creator: Nadia Tatiana García-Barrientos, Fabiola Solorzano-Ibarra, Ksenia Klimov-Kravtchenko, Jose Manuel Rojas-Diaz, Marcela Sofia Guitron-Aviña, Francisco Javier Ceja-Flores, Jose Alfonso Cruz-Ramos, Pablo Cesar Ortiz-Lazareno, Felipe de Jesús Bustos-Rodriguez, Juan Carlos Vazquez-Limon, Miriam Ruth Bueno
pmc-12651438.description: Simple SummaryImmune checkpoint inhibitor therapy is of growing importance for the treatment and management of cervical cancer. In this analysis of known and emerging inhibitory checkpoint receptors in patients with cervical cancer, we observed that in addition to an increase in PD-1 and TIGIT, the emerging receptors Tim-3, LAG-3 and NKG2A were likewise upregulated.

pmc-12860106.title: Contacts to general practitioners and renewal of antihypertensive medication - a four-year follow-up in primary health care, Turku, Finland
pmc-12860106.creator: Jouni K. Johansson, Päivi Korhonen
pmc-12860106.description: BackgroundPersistence with medication is central to the effectiveness of antihypertensive therapy.Electronic communication between patients and doctors may have potential to improve medication persistence among patients with hypertension. Our objective was to examine the use of antihypertensive medication in subjects with hypertension in primary health care in Finland in a longitudinal setting.

pmc-13050579.title: Comparing Warming Methods in the Trauma Bay: A Multi-center Cohort Study
pmc-13050579.creator: Gayla Miles, Kristi Bonny, Jacob Roden-Foreman
pmc-13050579.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDespite the clear link between hypothermia and poor outcomes, few studies have evaluated warming methods in the trauma bay. This study aimed to compare the effectiveness of three warming methods for full trauma activations arriving at the emergency department.MethodsA multi-site, retrospective cohort study was conducted at two Level I and one Level II trauma centers in North Texas, United States, from August 1, 2023, to July 31, 2024.

pmc-13273660.creator: Gabriel Kambale Bunduki

pmc-13331724.title: Integrative Multi‐Omics Analysis Reveals the Tumor‐Suppressive and Immunoregulatory Roles of SEMA5B in Prostate Cancer
pmc-13331724.creator: Zhiguo Fan, Yihaoyun Lou, Xuan Zhou, Guang Liu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yuanjie Tang, Zhen Zhu, Shancheng Ren, Yifan Chang
pmc-13331724.description: SEMA5B plays an important role in the maintenance of neural development and is highly environment dependent in tumorigenesis. The roles of SEMA5B in prostate cancer remain underexplored. This study investigates SEMA5B's functions in prostate cancer, revealing its role as a tumor suppressor transcriptionally regulated by androgen receptor and uncovering novel biomarkers and potential immunotherapeutic mechanisms.
